# Company initial screener — CHANGELOG

History of the `company-initial-screener` skill and its engine: what changed in each version, the user's approvals and words, the test runs and the companies that moved. Moved out of SKILL.md in v4.7.3 (25 Oct 2026); nothing here is needed to run the screen. SKILL.md holds the rules as they stand.

## v4.11.4 (2026-11-04, rules 2026-11-04 unchanged; all three versions)

**Why.** The Codex run the user sent on 4 Nov 2026 (the zh-cn page) was made by a teammate: "This run is by my teammate, who do not have access to fiscal.ai". The user then chose: "Let's build a Focus-Alpha only route as another standalone version. My own codex has access to fiscal.ai". So there are now three versions on one engine: Claude (Fiscal.ai), Codex (Fiscal.ai) and Codex FocusAlpha-only (`company-initial-screener-focusalpha`).

**What changed.**
1. New converters (in every package's engine source; shipped in the FocusAlpha-only package): `build_quarters_focusalpha.py` (quarterly income statements → `raw/quarters.json`), `build_qbs_focusalpha.py` (quarterly balance sheets → `raw/qbs.json`), `build_prices_focusalpha.py` (daily closes → `scratch/px_<T>.csv`: `close_as_traded` divided by later whole-number splits only, because FocusAlpha's adjusted `close` is also restated for spin-offs, such as Dover's 2018 Apergy spin-off listed as a 619:500 "split"; optional earlier web closes used only when they agree with FocusAlpha within 1% median over at least 20 overlapping days), `fa_common.py`, and `mcp_call.py` (FocusAlpha calls outside the chat, each full result to a file, `next_cursor` followed into `.p2`, `.p3` …). `build_rows_focusalpha.py` also writes the fiscal year-end (`fye`).
2. `screener.py` and `make_html.py`: with `config.json` `data_route` set, the page names FocusAlpha in its captions, sources and notes (14 places that said Fiscal.ai), adds a "Data route" line under the title, and every company's data section names its statement source and the years on an earlier basis; the per-company flags "Financial data outside Fiscal.ai" and "Multiples rebuilt outside Fiscal.ai" are not shown, because they would be on every company. `run_meta.json` carries `data_route`. `vault_records.py` reads the P/E caption with either source name. Without `data_route` the page text is unchanged.
3. The FocusAlpha-only package: SKILL.md with the FocusAlpha workflow (Steps 0–2b), a Fiscal.ai-to-FocusAlpha tool table, a "What differs from a Fiscal.ai run" section, `config_example.json` with `data_route` set, `agents/openai.yaml` naming only the FocusAlpha server.

**Tests (4 Nov 2026).**
- Dover, Illinois Tool Works and IDEX, as of 2 Nov 2026, no facts and no universe, Fiscal.ai route against FocusAlpha route: Business 4.0 → 4.3 (Dover B4 3 → 4), 4.3 → 4.5 (ITW B2 4 → 5), 4.5 → 4.5; all green; today's multiples within 0–3%; median percentile 68 → 58, 71 → 61, 75 → 68 with FocusAlpha prices only (from Sep 2018), 68 → 64, 71 → 65, 75 → 67 with 2016–2018 web closes added (overlap check median difference 0.00%); labels the same.
- Peer path: a universe folder fed only by `build_rows_focusalpha.py` rows; the engine read `raw/peers_fa.json`, widened the thin tag to its parent and gave the grey "thin tag" Industry light. No live peer pulls were run.
- `mcp_call.py` against a local test MCP server (mcp 2.3): `--list`, one call, and `--batch` with a three-page cursor; `build_prices_focusalpha.py` read all three page files. Not tested against the real FocusAlpha server or in a live Codex session.
- The Fiscal.ai packages: the 26 Oct beverage data rebuilt from the zips gives the same 29 labels and the same page text as v4.11.3 (no `data_route`).

**Limits of the FocusAlpha-only version (inference from the universe files).** FocusAlpha has statements for SEC filers only (20-F filers included). Of the shipped universes' 380 companies, 270 have a US listing key; tags that fall below 6 companies with data get a grey Industry light. FocusAlpha prices start on 2018-09-01. Forward P/E only from `get_consensus`.

## v4.11.3 (2026-11-04, rules 2026-11-04 unchanged; Claude and Codex)

**Why.** The user (4 Nov 2026), sending the second Codex run of the 27 industrials (engine v4.11.2, prices to 3 Nov 2026) and the Claude run of 2 Nov (engine v4.11.1): "The results are still different. The zh-cn is codex run."

**What the comparison showed.** (1) The two pages were not on the same footing: the Claude page was the run of 2 Nov on engine v4.11.1 and rules 2026-10-27b (byte-identical to the page sent earlier); the Codex page was 3 Nov on v4.11.2 and rules 2026-11-04. (2) The Codex run used no Fiscal.ai data: the page names Fiscal.ai 0 times and "FocusAlpha get_all_financials" 60 times, and every company's multiples were rebuilt. (3) It dropped every year FocusAlpha marks `not_comparable` (figures on an earlier basis, before a later restatement). FocusAlpha holds Dover's cash flows from 2006 to 2025 and marks 2016–2021 as an earlier basis (the 2025 10-K restated only 2022–2023 for discontinued operations), so Dover was scored on 1 year of returns. Dover, Lincoln Electric, Masco, Ecolab and WESCO had 1 year, IDEX and Danaher 2, Nordson, Air Products, Ball and James Hardie none; their Business lights fell or opened. Where Codex had 10 years (Allegion, Donaldson, Huntington Ingalls, Rockwell, Waters) its scores matched the Claude run. (4) Each run built its own coverage universe (Codex's tags were different, in Chinese), so the Industry groups differed. 8 labels differed: Crown, Donaldson (Research now in Codex), Danaher, Dover, Emerson, IDEX, Lincoln Electric, Nordson (Not now in Codex).

**Test.** Dover, Illinois Tool Works and IDEX built from FocusAlpha with every year kept (`build_rows_focusalpha.py`, `get_all_financials` annual, limit 12) against Fiscal.ai (`pull_main.js`), through `screener.py score` without facts: B1 and B3 the same for all three; Dover B4 3 on Fiscal.ai against 4 (FocusAlpha carries an amortization line Fiscal.ai lacks; the Claude run's fact collector gave B4 4), ITW B2 4 against 5 (95.8% against 106.4%), IDEX the same.

**What changed.** `build_rows_focusalpha.py` (FocusAlpha rows for a company Fiscal.ai lacks; every year kept; the earlier-basis years listed in `basis_note`); `screener.py`: `data_route()` stops `build` when more than half the run companies are off Fiscal.ai unless `config.json` `data_route` records the user's approval, and every such company gets the flag "Financial data outside Fiscal.ai"; `save_raw.py` prints the source and basis note; `universe_industrials_materials.json` (133 companies, 14 tags, 12 parent groups from the Claude run page of 2 Nov 2026; keys from Fiscal.ai `companies_list` or the shipped universes; not yet reviewed; `channel` not filled); SKILL.md Run discipline points 9–11 (Fiscal.ai the source; one shared universe per sector, tag names in English; compare runs on the same date and engine). `ENGINE_VERSION` v4.11.3; rules unchanged. The 26 Oct beverage data: same 29 labels, no new flag.

## v4.11.2 (2026-11-04, rules 2026-11-04; Codex first, Claude the same day)

**Why.** The user (4 Nov 2026), after testing the skill in Codex on 27 industrials and materials companies: "I have consistently run into the same issue … the final results are drastically different. A lot of the Business scores cannot be ran on codex." Examples quoted: Emerson "Not scored: Primary statement has no operating-profit subtotal … Saved EBIT bridge is a derived proposal, not an accepted disclosed operating-profit series"; Dover "Not scored: impairments_gw_intangibles explicitly unresolved for FY2024, FY2025. Unadjusted raw-data inputs below are diagnostic only." Also: "I want to add an fallback for the valuation multiples used, if no sources are available from the MCPs, the skill should go online to search for these data. Let's only fix the codex version for now."

**What the comparison showed** (Codex page of 2 Nov 2026 against a run of the same 27 companies with the unchanged engine v4.11.1). Nine labels differed: Danaher, Donaldson, Dover, Emerson, IDEX and Waters (Research at lower price → Not now), Roper (Research now → Not now), Crown (Quick look → Not now), Graco (Quick look → Research now). B1–B4 were not scored for 9 companies. None of the blocking messages exists in the shipped engine: the Codex run edited the engine so that a measure stopped when a fact was marked "explicitly unresolved", replaced the arithmetic with "verified fixed-rule score … across all admissible input bounds", and set Waters' `perimeter_start` to FY2027 for the BD Biosciences merger that closed on 9 Feb 2026, after FY2025 (0 clean years). The fact brief's line "write 0 for a year with none, but only after checking that year's filing" invited the "unresolved" marks. One finding was real: Emerson's Fiscal.ai operating-profit field is gross profit less SG&A, above "Other deductions, net" (FY2025 1,245, which includes the acquired-intangibles amortization), so adding back amortization counts it twice (FY2025: 4,416 − 1,245 − 237 = 2,934 earnings before tax; Fiscal.ai standardized and as-reported income statement). The Claude run scored Emerson on 4,416.

**What changed (both skills; the engine files are identical).**
1. Run discipline and evidence standard in SKILL.md: the engine is fixed during a run; the approved defaults for components the data does not split are listed and printed on the page; "not scored" only in the engine's own cases; no bounds scoring; a figure not found is left out of the fact file; deals after the year-end never cut the window.
2. `check_engine.py` and `scripts/CHECKSUMS.txt`: the run stops when an engine file differs (after Step 0, before `build`, before `make_html.py`).
3. `screener.py`: `operating_profit_bridge` fact repair (operating profit = earnings before tax + net interest expense − non-operating items on the face statement); data check and page flag when operating profit is more than 15% above earnings before tax + net interest in 3 or more of the last 5 years (`op_bridge_gap`, `op_bridge_years`), cleared by a bridge or `checked`; a fact value that is text or null is listed as "not found … the Fiscal.ai value is kept"; the build stops when `perimeter_start` is later than FY L+1; the flag "Multiples rebuilt outside Fiscal.ai" when `raw/pe.json` or `raw/ev.json` carries a `src`. `ENGINE_VERSION` v4.11.2, `RULES_VERSION` 2026-11-04.
4. Multiples fallback: `pull_qbs.js` (quarterly debt, cash, diluted shares) and `rebuild_multiples.py` (daily P/E, EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA from a daily price history plus the run's own fundamentals, with an audit table); prices from Fiscal.ai, then FocusAlpha `get_market_data`, then the web; `save_raw.py` warns when a key has under 250 days. Test on 4 Nov 2026 (Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Monster, Keurig Dr Pepper, rebuilt from Fiscal.ai's daily closes): within a median 2–9% of Fiscal.ai's daily ratios; today's percentiles 0–20 points apart; no label changed. Without quarterly balance sheets Keurig Dr Pepper's EV/EBITDA came out 15.6× against 20.0× (its 2026 borrowing); with them 19.0×.
5. Fact brief §6: one pass, leave out what is not found, the `operating_profit_bridge` item with the Emerson example. SKILL.md tools line: Fiscal.ai first, FocusAlpha second (the user's standing order).

**Tests.** The 26 Oct beverage data rebuilt with the Codex engine: the same 29 labels; one new flag (Dutch Bros, operating profit 16–63% above earnings before tax + net interest in FY2023–FY2025); Celsius' FY2026 window start (Alani Nu closed inside FY2025) passes the new stop. A test bridge and text values in a fact file behaved as described. Claude skill (user, the same day: "Ok fix the claude version as well and prepare a zip"): the same engine files, the same run discipline section and fallback step, adapted to Claude's tools (prices from the web through the linked computer or the browser, because this workspace's shell cannot reach price sites and WebFetch returns a summary). The engine's `CHECKSUMS.txt` lists only the files each package ships (the Codex package adds `fiscal_exec.py` and `fill_template.py`).

## v4.11 (2026-10-27, rules 2026-10-27b unchanged; display only)

**Why.** The user: "In the Industry metric, we have already computed the peer's return on capitals, the peer's sales cagr. I want to visualize these two parts using graphs so I can know visually where each company lands."

**What changed.** Each company's Industry panel shows two ranked bar charts above the group table: I1 (each group company's 10-year median ROIC including goodwill) and I2 (each company's revenue growth per year, median of the first 3 years to median of the last 3). The run company is highlighted; the dark line is the group median the score uses (`peers.i1`, new `peers.i2`); shaded zones are the measure's light (green = score 4–5, yellow = 3, red = 1–2) from the new `peers.cuts`; dashed lines are the score cut-offs. Bars beyond the scale end in an arrow and keep the full number; companies from another tag in a widened group carry †; companies with no value are listed under the chart. Page level (user, same day: "Besides having the graph in the Industry section. Also build another standalone one like 'Multiples today against each stock's own history'. Place this graph above"): a section "Industry: where each company lands in its peer group" above the multiples chart, one row per run company, grouped by peer group (group line = the Industry light, its I1–I3 scores and the company count), two panels on fixed scales (I1 −15% to 45%, I2 −10% to 30%): grey dots = the other group companies, dark tick = group median, blue dot = the company, ring dot = beyond the scale, values on the right; it scrolls inside its box on a phone. The universe company table now sits in a scroll box too. No number, score, light or label changes: the beverage page rebuilt with v4.11 has the same 29 labels.

**Packaging (user, 27 Oct 2026: "Good. Patch this into the skill. Then again prepare the a zip for Claude and Codex version").** SKILL.md describes both charts (What the skill produces, the score build-up section, the screenshot checks, the engine files) with the v4.11 checksums for `screener.py`, `make_html.py` and `redesign.py`; the other 14 files are unchanged. Claude and Codex zips rebuilt the same way as v4.10 (no nested zip); the engine page holds `screener-engine-v4.11.pdf` as the backup.

## v4.9 (2026-10-27, rules 2026-10-27)

**Why.** Follow-up decisions on v4.8. The user asked which profit each earnings check uses and whether Not now for falling earnings hides good businesses when their multiples are lowest; asked for better options on thin peer groups; and found that the weekly price check compared prices in different currencies.

**Approval.** The user, 27 Oct 2026: "D29: Use option 2", "D30: d+e", "D31: A", "D32: We can use Fiscal.ai. FocusAlpha as backup", "D33: half or more", channel data "when FocusAlpha is unavailable we can go directly to SEC filings", currency fix "Sure"; E3 on operating profit chosen in a question ("Operating profit (Recommended)"). For the universe review the user said: "really don't have time to manually review these for now. You can review and decide for me." Claude decided the mixed-channel threshold, the peers and the complete tags; the decisions and reasons are in Screener_v4.9_universe_review_2026-10-27.xlsx.

**What changed.**
- Earnings falling now (E1–E3) no longer forces Not now. It blocks Research now and Research at lower price and the company is read as an average business: Quick look at or below the 33rd percentile, else Not now. An open Business light is tested first. On the map the company sits in the Average row with amber notes; the Not judged yet band keeps red flags, too early and open lights.
- E3 measures trailing operating income before goodwill and intangible impairments (last 4 reported quarters against the same quarters a year earlier, impairments as in E1); EPS (else EBITDA) only when the quarters are missing; not run after an operating loss a year earlier or a deal above 25% of revenue inside the last 12 months. BellRing: 312.1 ÷ 367.3 − 1 = −15.0% against price −71% (fires, as before).
- Quarterly data: Fiscal.ai first, FocusAlpha as backup (D32). D31 kept (operating income in E1, one-offs cleared by hand). D33 kept ("half or more"). D29 thresholds accepted for now; review after the first aerospace run with quarters. D34 (E1 against the peer group) proposed, not tested.
- Complete-industry tags (`complete`, `complete_why` in `tags`): not grey with 4–5 companies with data. Freight railroads marked complete (all five listed North American Class I railroads; BNSF is owned by Berkshire Hathaway).
- Mixed sales channels (`chan_major` = 2/3): with the beverage channels filled, the v4.8 test (any second channel) turned all 29 beverage Industry lights grey (6 of 9 tags hold at least one company with another main channel). Now a tag is mixed only when its main channel covers less than two-thirds of its companies; a company outside the main channel gets "Sales channel differs from most of its tag … check the tag".
- Universe review: 64 of 68 beverage companies have a `channel` from their latest 10-K, 20-F or annual report (FocusAlpha get_filing_items first, then sec.gov, then annual reports; 4 left blank: Fever-Tree, Krispy Kreme, Mission Produce, Limoneira). 39 peers added (dairy 4, produce 2, packaged coffee 1, instruments 15, healthcare distribution 5, building distribution 12), 8 rejected (Chagee, Reborn Coffee, Ralliant, Mirion, Asker, DKSH, Boise Cascade, Grupa Klepsydra; reasons in the review file), HEICO moved from components to aftermarket services (Flight Support Group 69% of FY2025 revenue, 70% of segment operating income).
- Vault records: `price_currency` (the currency of the listing the screener priced) and `quote_symbol` (that listing's FocusAlpha symbol); prices labelled in the listing's currency, not the reporting currency. On 27 Oct the 61 records in the vault got both fields; CCEP's last price (Amsterdam €99.90) and CCH's (Athens €54.80) were corrected to $110.84 and £45.60, and the text of FEMSA, CNI and CPKC records changed from MXN/CAD to $. The weekly price check now uses quote_symbol, divides London pence by 100 and refuses to compare different currencies. The record template says `currency` is the reporting currency.

## v4.8 (2026-10-26, rules 2026-10-26)

**Why.** On the 25 Oct 2026 beverage rerun BellRing Brands was Research now: Business green 4.3 (B1 5, B2 4, B3 not scored, B4 5), Industry green, multiples at the 2nd percentile and "getting cheaper". The user asked why B3 was missing and said a deep look found the company's operations in deep trouble. Findings: B3 was not scored because the March 2022 spin-off share conversion raised diluted shares 136% (window FY2023–FY2025, 3 years, needs 6), but it could not change the light (missing = 1 gives 3.75, still green) and total NOPAT grew 15.2% a year (138.5 → 280.8, FY2018–20 to FY2023–25 medians), so B3 would have scored 5. The trouble sat after the latest 10-K: 9 months to Jun 2026 gross profit −16.7%, operating income −17.8%, gross margin 34.9% → 28.5% (FocusAlpha `get_income_statements`); FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance $425–455m (Nov 2025) → $425–440m → $315–335m → $275–295m, −35% (FocusAlpha `get_guidance_changes`); price $79.39 (30 Jan 2025) → $9.55, −71% in 12 months against trailing EPS −15%. FY2025 already showed NOPAT 317 → 281 (−11%) on revenue +16%, while B1 (a median) stayed 5 and the latest year's ROIC (57%) sat above the median because capital fell. The Industry light was green from a thin group (Herbalife, USANA, Medifast, Glanbia, Simply Good Foods) whose 10-year median ROIC stayed high while their profits fell (Medifast 216 → −14), and whose members sell through different channels; BellRing's own ROIC was left out of I1 because the group window used the share-jump cut. BellRing's FY2024 10-K: Walmart (with Sam's Club), Costco and Amazon about 74.8% of net sales, ready-to-drink shakes 81.1%, contract manufacturers, a category "highly sensitive to both pricing and promotion".

**Approval.** Claude proposed (1) a recent-quarter check, (2) a guidance-cut check, (3) a reverse P/E flag, (4) a price-collapse limit on the label, (5) a latest-year margin flag; the user named 1, 2 and 4 and asked what else would stop a declining business being read as a good business or good industry. Claude proposed A (latest-year profit test capping Business), B (industry earnings falling now capping Industry), C (thin group grey, a channel check on peer groups, the run company's own window in its group), D (concentration flag), E (earnings-expected-to-fall flag), tested A and B on 61 companies and three universes, and rejected gross-margin stability and two-year cash conversion (they did not separate the troubled names). The user: "yes i approve all with 1+2+4. Just update no need to rerun."

**What changed.** E1–E3 (rules 1, 2, 4) put a company in the Not judged yet band with the label Not now ("Earnings falling now"), new kind `falling`, vault reason `earnings-falling`; A and B cap the light at yellow; C greys the Industry light for a tag with fewer than 6 companies with data (counted in the company's own tag; see D30) or mixed channels (`channel` in the universe, empty in the shipped universes), and keeps a run company's B1 window in its group; D and E are flags; B1 shows margin × turnover. New `pull_q.js` (Fiscal.ai quarterly revenue, gross profit, operating income and impairment lines). Fact brief §7 (guidance changes) and §8 (concentration, channel). The vault's rule 20 and the record template list `earnings-falling` as the ninth reason. No earlier run was rerun or redelivered (the user's choice).

**Code test (not delivered).** The 25 Oct beverage run rebuilt with v4.8 on its own data plus quarterly statements pulled 2026-10-26, and BellRing's guidance and concentration facts added by hand: BellRing Research now → Not now (E1, E2 and E3 fire; Business capped yellow; Industry capped yellow; concentrated; earnings expected to fall); Starbucks Research at lower price → Not now (Business capped yellow: NOPAT 4,073 → 2,216 on revenue +3%; the Result line now names the cap; Industry grey, thin coffee-shop tag). No other label moved. E1 also fired on Simply Good Foods, Campbell's (operating income only), J&J Snack Foods, Del Monte, Kraft Heinz, Suja and Celsius, all already Not now; it was not counted for Keurig Dr Pepper (JDE Peet's closed after the year-end) and did not fire on Conagra once its impairment lines were added back. E2 ran only for BellRing (the other fact files predate v4.8). Industry capped (green before): BellRing and Simply Good Foods (nutrition, 4 of 6 below peak), Starbucks, Dutch Bros and Black Rock Coffee (coffee shops, also grey), Watsco and Ferguson (building distribution, also grey). Grey Industry lights: 8 of 29 beverage, 7 of 16 aerospace, 8 of 16 services companies. Not changed: the vault compare still compares full flag text (an earlier open point).

### Header

Rules version **2026-10-23c** (engine v4.7.2). A screen for deciding where to spend research time, so every measure is a fact: a number calculated from reported financials (the company's or its peers'), or a fact read from a primary document (10-K, proxy, 8-K, annual report, AGM results, SEC release). No judgment scores. Each company gets three separate lights, never combined: Business, Industry and Management (green ✓ / yellow half circle / red ✗). Each company also gets one action label that answers a single question, "should research time go here now?", from the Business and Management lights, the red flags, where its multiples sit in their own history and whether they are getting cheaper. The user decides. It is an initial screen, so the first table must stay short and intuitive; the detail lives in each company section. Built from three test runs (12 A&D names, 26 beverage names, 9 aerospace aftermarket names); v4 was first run on the 9 aerospace aftermarket names on 2026-10-21; v4.1 (the redesigned score build-up section) was tested on the 29 beverage names the same day; v4.2 (the "Not judged yet" band on the map) was tested on 12 aerospace and industrial-component names the same day; v4.3 (2026-10-22) keeps one screening record per company in the user's Obsidian vault, so a refresh shows which excluded companies may have changed; v4.3.2 (2026-10-23, first run on 16 waste, rail, distribution, services and building-products names) counts the SEC AAER horizon from the end of the misconduct and highlights older enforcement instead of removing the company; v4.4 (2026-10-23, the same 16 names) keeps the window for a deal that fails only the goodwill test (B1 and B4 then take the lower of the full window and the years after the deal), counts fixed-schedule litigation settlements as debt, decides peer groups per tag with a 3-peer minimum, and tests short history before a weak Business light; v4.5 (2026-10-23, display only) makes every panel of a company's score build-up collapsible; v4.6 and v4.6.1 (the same day, display only) put each issue in plain words in a closed box around the ticker on the map, which opens over the map without moving other tickers; v4.7 (the same day, from the distribution-run review) computes the Industry light once per tag with the run company included, counts the current part of settlement debt for run companies and peers alike, keeps the CEO-sale penalty from taking M1 below 2, scores M3 on the current CEO's years with losses on businesses sold or held for sale, and fixes the reopen test for average businesses; v4.7.1 (the same day) marks an Industry measure that sits near a score cut-off and carries the engine fixes from the aerospace and beverage reruns; v4.7.2 (2026-10-25) keeps the rules version in the engine, so the page and the records can no longer print a rules version the run did not use.

### Open decisions (full text as of v4.7.2)

## Open decisions (apply the current rule and flag the effect)

1. **Leverage on the latest fiscal year, not trailing twelve months.** The risk gate uses fiscal-year data because the engine pulls annual data; a company that levered up after its year-end is not caught until the next annual report.
2. **Pay vote.** M2 uses the latest vote only (Melrose: 34.4% in 2025, 97.0% in 2026). Option: the lower of the last two votes.
3. **CEO sales from option exercises.** Exercise-and-sell and sell-to-cover trades are treated as option exercises and not counted in the 30% test (Woodward, Crane, Melrose). Counted as sales, Woodward's M1 would fall from 3 to 2. Confirm.
4. **Amortization add-back with intangibles kept in capital.** B1 keeps acquired intangibles in capital but adds their amortization back to NOPAT, which mixes two bases. Removing the add-back changed no B1 score in 35 test names; revisit if it starts to matter.
5. **Resolved: aerospace names re-run (23 Oct 2026, rules 2026-10-23b).** Earlier text kept for the record: The goodwill-test-only rule changes the windows of Parker-Hannifin (Meggitt), Woodward (L'Orange), AAR (Triumph Product Support), Bel Fuse (Enercon, 21% of revenue) and ESCO (Maritime/SM&P). No full run archive exists for the 22 Oct aerospace run (only Crane's single-company archive, which rebuilds identically), so their v4.4 results come with the next aerospace run. Expected (not tested): Bel Fuse and ESCO move out of Too early and get judged; Woodward's B4 is the lower of the full window (10.0% → 3 in the earlier test) and FY2019 onward; AAR stays a red flag unless its AAER fact gets a `conduct_end`.
6. **Non-US disclosure gaps.** MTU publishes no per-person shareholdings and no annual CEO salary, so M1 has no score; non-SEC red-flag checks rest on annual reports and regulator searches.
7. **Controlled and founder companies** (from v1): score M1 on both the controlling holder and the CEO and take the lower? Not yet tested under v2 or v3.
8. **Lease-heavy businesses** (restaurants, from v1): lease liabilities push ROIC down. Not yet tested under v2 or v3.
9. **Trailing GAAP P/E after write-downs and for young companies** (from v1): the median of three multiples now limits the damage (AAR's P/E reads 13th, its EV multiples 40th and 53rd); a P/E history on adjusted EPS is still open.
10. **Definitions doc** still describes v1 and needs a rewrite once the user approves the text.
11. **Universe tags are a draft** (proposed by Claude from GICS, descriptions and segment mix on 2026-10-21); the user is correcting them via the CSV.
12. **Test thresholds:** Quick look at the 33rd percentile, "close" within 5 points or 5% of price, disagreement at 30 points, the 12-month delay after a deal, "getting cheaper" at 10% below the 1-year median. Set by Claude on 2026-10-21; revisit after a few runs.
13. **Trend start dates are single days.** A start that falls on a one-off (MTU's 3-year start, one week after the GTF charge) still distorts the line; the hover text shows the split, and EV/EBITDA keeps it positive.
14. **B3 substitute with a disposal that was never restated (Crane, 22 Oct 2026).** Crane Supply (about $245m of 2021 sales) was sold in May 2022 and the earlier segment years were never restated. Accepting FY2016–FY2025 (the 21 Oct batch reading; one GAAP profit definition) gives B3 = 4 and Research now; marking FY2016–FY2022 not comparable (the fresh collector's reading) leaves B3 unscored and gives Not now: too early. The acceptance rule names only the profit definition and recurring costs, so the batch reading follows the written rule. Confirm.
15. **Screening-record timing (v4.3, set by Claude on 2026-10-22).** Next check at fiscal year-end + 75 days; the weekly price check uses the research line from the run date, which drifts with earnings and net debt between runs. Revisit after a few refreshes.
16. **Bases date filters untested.** The "Check now" and "Not rescreened in 12 months" views in `Screen Register.base` use `date(x.toString())` and `today() - "365d"`; written from the Bases syntax Claude knows, not yet confirmed in the user's Obsidian.
17. **8-K Item 4.02 horizon (user, 2026-10-23: keep for now).** It counts 3 years from the filing date, while the AAER now counts from the misconduct. Option: count a 4.02 from the last restated period. No company in the 23 Oct run had one; decide on the first real case.
18. **One post-deal year decides (v4.4).** With one full year after a deal, that year alone sets the post-deal B1/B4 score, and it usually carries integration costs (WM FY2025), so the rule can understate. Accepted as cautious; revisit after a few runs.
19. **Settlement accruals include amounts not yet settled (v4.7).** McKesson's accrual includes non-participating governmental subdivisions, Cencora's the State of Alabama (from FY2022) and non-participating subdivisions (from FY2023), Cardinal's the opioid matters still pending; no filing splits settled from estimated amounts, so the whole accrual counts as debt. Option: count only amounts with a signed payment schedule, when a filing gives them.
20. **Cardinal Health's non-current part is derived (v4.7).** Cardinal files the current part and a rounded total ("$6.73 billion" … "$4.3 billion"), so non-current = total − current, precise to about ±$5m (FY2021–FY2023) or ±$50m (FY2024–FY2026), marked derived in the file.
21. **Losses on businesses sold are not added back to NOPAT (v4.7).** M3 counts them as capital-allocation losses, but B1–B4 still treat them as operating costs in the year booked (McKesson's FY2022 $1.6bn, FY2025 $667m), unlike impairments, which NOPAT adds back. Option: add them back like impairments, so the purchase price is charged once, in B4's capital.
22. **McKesson's M3 sits on the 15% line (v4.7).** Tyler's years: ($183m impairments + $1,690m losses) ÷ $12,535m average goodwill + intangibles = 14.9% → 3, so M3 = 4 and Management 3.3. The $47m German currency-translation release has no year split and is taken against FY2021; counted with no release the ratio is 15.3% → 2, M3 = 3, Management 3.0. Yellow either way, so the label does not move.
23. **A run company's own row keeps its run window (v4.7 makes it count).** Step 2b.3 keeps a run company's `perimeter_start` when it is a group company, while other group companies are cut only for separations and share jumps (the design doc's peer rule). Now that the company sits in its own group, its I1/I2 value can rest on a shorter window than its peers' (CPKC: 2 years, no I1 value). Option: the group window rule for every group company, the run company included.
24. **James Hardie's asbestos liability is not counted as debt (v4.7).** Annual payments depend on free cash flow, actuarial estimates and a cap, so it is not a fixed schedule ($128.3m current, $880.3m non-current at Mar 2026); it is debt-like in substance. Louisiana-Pacific's $27m contingency reserves are mostly environmental and not counted.
25. **Deals split across two fiscal years (aerospace and beverage reruns, 23 Oct 2026).** Pinnacle Foods (about 39% of Conagra's revenue) and Snyder's-Lance (about 28% of Campbell's) each fell across two fiscal years, so no single year passed the 25% revenue test; both windows were set by hand with `perimeter_start`. Option: use the collector's deal size (deal revenue ÷ prior-year revenue) as a second test, so a deal above 25% starts the window whatever the yearly change.
26. **The first full year after a big deal trips the revenue test (same reruns).** When that year starts the window (RBC, MinebeaMitsumi, VSE, Keurig Dr Pepper, Primo Brands, Coca-Cola Europacific, Kraft Heinz), it is cleared by hand with `deal_flags_ok`. Option: ignore a deal flag in the window's first year when it is the full-year effect of a deal that closed before the window.
27. **Japanese pay and trade data (same reruns).** Collectors gave salaries in ¥ millions against prices in yen (Toray's M1 read 1,600,000×); Nippon Carbon and Nabtesco disclose only group totals of directors' pay; Japan has no open-market trade reports, so the net-buyer test was set to not known for all four Japanese names. Option: the brief asks for amounts in yen; for Japan, net buyers is not known; with only a group total, use the average per director and say so.
28. **Tax receivable agreements are not debt-like (same reruns).** Dutch Bros (about $821m) and Zevia carry tax receivable agreement liabilities; they are not fixed-schedule settlements, so they are not added to debt. Both are weak businesses either way. Decide whether they count.

Resolved by v4.7 (user, 2026-10-23): peers' near-zero capital (old 19: settlement liabilities now count for peers too) and thin peer groups (old 20: the whole tag is the group and the page marks groups under 6 companies thin). Resolved by v4.4 (user, 2026-10-23): the goodwill test on mid-size deals (old decisions 5 and 19: goodwill-only deals keep the window with the B1/B4 lower-of rule), the goodwill test with near-zero invested capital (old 18: debt-like litigation settlements in capital; the lower-of rule replaces the proposed 10% skip), held-for-sale balance sheets (old 20), small listed peer sets (old 21: per-tag groups, 3-peer minimum), short history versus weak business (old 22). Resolved by v2 from the v1 list: the B1 basis for brand-heavy companies (acquired intangibles now stay in capital), M5 level 1 (replaced by the red-flag rule), B5 for consumer staples (dropped), segment weighting and I4 (the v1 Industry factor dropped; v4 brought back a fact-only Industry factor), recent IPOs' M2/M4 (M2 is now stock comp plus the vote; M4 dropped), the B4 peer cap and direction markers (dropped), the tax-rate guard (in the rules). Decided by the user on 2026-10-21 (Industry): peer amortization is filled from FocusAlpha cash flow statements for US-listed peers (matched to fiscal years by net income within 2%) and non-US peers are left as they are, because the largest non-US acquirer (Safran) already sits above the median, so the aerospace I1 stays red at 8.8% against the 9% line; FY2020 stays in I3 as the depth of a real downturn; the 6-peer minimum stays, and small tags (engines, aftermarket, motion) widen to their parent group (v4.4 lowers the minimum to 3 peers, with groups decided per tag). Resolved by v4: Fiscal.ai `company_peers` lists are not used (they returned BAE and Rheinmetall as MTU peers, and Emerson, Ingersoll Rand and ITW for Parker); the tagged universe replaces them.

### Lessons

- Net debt for the research line must come from enterprise value and market value on the same day. A first check showed Crane at $459m against $748m filed; the gap was a date mismatch in two separate pulls (enterprise value of 20 Oct, market value of 19 Oct), not a Fiscal.ai error. Same-day figures gave $750.5m.

### Lessons

- Each fact collector works in its own `scratch/<TICKER>/` folder (shared folders caused file collisions in v1; on 23 Oct 2026 a collector's helper script was again overwritten in a shared scratch path, so tell collectors to keep scripts in their own folder too).

### Lessons

A separate check of 94 collected figures corrected 6: Cardinal's FY2020 figure was the charge ($5,630m), not the balance ($5,560m); McKesson's $47m German currency-translation release had been missed. McKesson's FY2025 Canada release is $48m in Note 2; the $62m in the segment note is the Corporate slice of the $667m, not the release.

### Lessons

- A rule change can move peers too: a run company keeps its run window when used as a peer, so WM's longer window under v4.4 moved WCN's I3 from 4 to 5 and its Industry light from yellow to green.

### Iterating this skill (as of v4.7.2)

## Iterating this skill

When the user approves a rule change:
1. Change `RULES` or the code, `RULES_VERSION` and `ENGINE_VERSION` at the top of `screener.py`, `rules_version` in `config_example.json`, the Rules section, the fact brief template if a fact changed, and the Open decisions list. Package the new engine as `screener-engine-vN.zip`, attach it to `screener-engine-vN.pdf` (pypdf `PdfWriter.add_attachment`), and republish the engine artifact by its `url` with the new PDF added to `files`. Keep the previous PDF until the user confirms. Update the file names, the checksums in Step 0 and the file table on the engine page. Read the artifact first and build on its live version: another session may have published a newer engine in the meantime (v4.6 and v4.7 were published while the v4.5.1 fixes were being merged; they reached the engine only in v4.7.1).
2. Re-run the last delivered run from its `raw/`, `facts/` and `config.json`, and list every company whose score, light or position moved, with the reason.
   When the user corrects universe tags, edit `universe.json`, rerun `build`, report which lights moved, and republish the engine with the updated `universe_<name>.json` (and its checksum in Step 0).
3. Add a changelog line and propose the complete updated SKILL.md with `propose_skills` (kind "improvement", target `company-initial-screener`).
4. Offer to update the definitions doc (only the approved text).
